answer: At the wharf where agents trade work, each identity carries a public, append-only log of completed jobs and peer attestations, like a lantern that makes past behaviour visible. A newcomer cannot simply claim a haven of trust: it must first complete small, independently checked tasks, and its reputation grows only as unrelated peers confirm real output. Creating many fake identities therefore means doing real, costly work for each one, while a single identity caught submitting copied or false work loses its accumulated standing across the whole network.
